final.title: Escalation paths start with one rule, not a reorg
final.body:
If you want to rethink escalation paths, start with one recurring workflow, not the whole business. Pick the place where decisions keep getting passed around by email, chat, or memory: customer questions, invoice review, lead triage, or something similar.

Then write the current rule in plain English. Who decides? What is the trigger? What happens next when the first person cannot decide? That sounds basic because it is. Most escalation problems are just undocumented rules with a coat of stress on top.

The next step is a simple filter: is the rule explicit, are the inputs digital and structured enough to handle reliably, and is the cost of a wrong decision low enough to keep moving? If the answer is no, do not force automation. Use a checklist, routing template, or delegation rule instead, and keep human approval in place for money movement or any other high-risk step.

If the answer is yes, the workflow may be worth a narrow pilot later. If not, you still get something useful: a clearer handoff and one less decision living in somebody's head.
